symptom: `create javascript action M.JSA (S: StringTemplate(Text))` passes check and exec. On main the parameter is silently written as a String (describe: `S: String`); after the Java-action StringTemplate fix it was written as a CodeActions$StringTemplateParameterType into the JavaScript action. mx check 11.13 reports 0 errors for both
cause: The grammar's dataType accepts StringTemplate(...) for Java and JavaScript actions alike, and both create handlers share astDataTypeToJavaActionParamType; nothing said a text template is a Java action type only
file: `mdl/executor/validate_javascript_action_types.go` (`unsupportedJavaScriptActionTypes`, the one decision; `validateJavaScriptActionTypes` = MDL-JSA01 in the no-project tier via validate_program.go); exec refuses in `execCreateJavaScriptAction`; test `mdl/executor/cmd_javascript_actions_string_template_test.go`; fixture `mdl-examples/bug-tests/javascript-action-1451-string-template.fail.mdl`
insight: **Fixing a shared converter widens what every caller accepts.** Teaching astDataTypeToJavaActionParamType StringTemplate for Java actions also made JavaScript actions write one — the twin of the twin-builder lesson (#1137) in the other direction: when a converter is shared, ask which caller must refuse the new case. mx check is no gate here (0 errors on main and on the branch), so the refusal has to be mxcli's; it needs no project, so it lives in the no-project tier and exec's pre-flight refuses it before anything is written. Document(...) has no MDL spelling, so the parser already refuses it for either kind of action. The return type is refused too: the return converter's default turned StringTemplate into Boolean
